This involves quantifying the additional risk introduced by each new service category (IAM, secrets, retention) and establishing a threshold where the marginal cost exceeds the marginal benefit for a preview-stage project. The primitives formalize this as a constraint satisfaction problem: given current architectural assumptions, adding Amplify services violates the principle of least privilege and increases the attack surface. The adoption trigger acts as a gatekeeper, ensuring that any backend expansion undergoes rigorous scrutiny before deployment.
